caption: Turns out the store cards weren't my real problem — the 27% loan was. Anyone else paying off the wrong debt first?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R21 500
p/m salary
Living in Kroonstad
slides.body:
Male, 30
Single, no kids
Job: Panel beater at a body shop
Net salary: R21 500 p/m

slides.title: Personal loan
slides.includes: R42 000 taken out for a paint job on my own car that turned into more
slides.body: This is the expensive one, 27% interest. It's first in line.

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: Room in a shared house near the workshop
slides.body: Cheap by choice. Every spare rand is going to the debt right now.

slides.title: Store cards
slides.includes: Two clothing accounts, both almost closed
slides.body: I opened these at 19 for outfits I don't even remember.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.body: I've cut this harder than anything else to speed up the loan.

slides.title: Transport
slides.includes: Taxi and the odd Uber on late finishes
slides.body: The workshop's outside town, there's no way around this one.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Cellphone, funeral policy, work boots & overalls, insurance on my own car, a small stokvel
slides.body: Ordinary life still costs money while you're paying off the extraordinary stuff.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R21 500. Whatever's left goes straight onto the loan, not into my pocket. Eleven months to go.

slides.title: I can finally see the finish line
slides.body:
I put every debt into Beyond Horizon and it worked out that clearing the personal loan first, not the store cards, saves me the most in interest.

Eleven months, not the sixteen I was on track for.

No bank login needed.
